findings.conclusion: All joint variants reproduce the frozen flat final trees, paths and authority on the same development cohort. This eliminates the earlier selected-tree PIP gap while reducing work versus enumerated candidates. Joint search still costs more than flat and does not establish physical QoR or hardware acceleration.

limitations: Single fixed 70-net development cohort, no held-out or full-design generalization.
Available boundary resources must have at most two SLR memberships; other catalogs are rejected explicitly.
Minimum cost is only within the fixed die order under a completed search. Other die orders, reentry and global shared-tree optimality are not covered.

Two early invocations finish with budget_exhausted even after flat fallback, then succeed in constrained retries after tree growth. Current trace does not separately encode the earlier discovery failure status or work split.
Byte equality is to the initial flat rerouting proposal, not the later hold-repaired tree. No fresh DCP/STA/DRC/bus-skew/bitstream signoff was run.
No concurrent die-local authority, HBM data plane, strict distributed reservation grant, or board latency/energy evidence.
next_work: Record discovery status/work separately and test deferring budget-limited attempts until the shared tree grows, while retaining an eventual full-graph rescue when progress stops.
